A small, beautiful cave.
A room. In a cave, a large open space.
A long, narrow way through.
A long hole under the ground that you can go through.
A deep, narrow hole that goes straight down.
A long, narrow crack in rock.
A thin crack in a rock.
A very deep, wide crack in the ground.
A hole so deep that it seems to have no bottom.
The opening of a cave.
A high, arched roof.
Spikes of rock that hang down from the roof of a cave.
Spikes of rock that rise from the floor of a cave.
Small, clear, shiny stones with flat sides.
A small area of still water.
Broken pieces of rock and stone.
The state of having no light.
Dim, shadowy half-darkness.
A sound that bounces back so you hear it again.

With drops of water falling from it.

verbs.explanation: Dug or pushed a way deep into something.
Bent one way and then another.
Ran slowly in a thin line.
Burned weakly and unsteadily, about to go out.
Shone with a faint, unsteady light.
Was fixed at the top and reached down.
Made something vanish, as if eating it.
Forced a way through a very small space.
Felt about with the hands, unable to see.
Slowly became quieter until it was gone.
Pushed tightly into a narrow space.
Moved along on hands and knees.
Flowed fast in a great mass.
Covered closely, like a knife in its case.

verbs.text: Exhaled a breath of cold air
Swallowed the beam of his torch

sentences.text: The dark, yawning mouth of the cave exhaled a breath of cold air that smelled of wet stone.
A narrow, winding passage burrowed deep into the hillside, sloping always downwards.
The tunnel opened without warning into a vast, vaulted cavern, tall as a cathedral and twice as silent.
Icy water dripped from the roof with the slow persistence of a clock.
Their voices reverberated through the tunnels long after they had fallen silent.
A few metres ahead, dense, impenetrable darkness swallowed the beam of his torch.
Slender, dripping stalactites hung from the vault like the pipes of a drowned organ.
Tiny, glittering crystals glimmered in the torchlight, a frost that had never melted.
As the passage narrowed, the cold, clammy walls closed in around them until each breath felt borrowed.
One by one they squeezed through the fissure and dropped into the chamber beyond.
The passage twisted and forked until they were lost in a bewildering labyrinth of tunnels.
Beyond the pool, the floor descended into blackness so complete that it seemed solid.
The candle guttered and died, and the dark rushed in like water.
A cloud of bats fluttered past her face, their wings as dry as paper.
Water trickled down the walls and gathered in hollows in the rough, uneven floor.
He groped along the wall, reading the rock with his fingertips as a blind man reads a page.
At the heart of the cave a still, glassy pool glowed faintly in the dark, undisturbed for centuries.
The last drip faded into silence, and the cold, sepulchral chamber felt like the loneliest place on earth.
They crawled beneath a low, jagged roof that snatched at their helmets.
Far below, a roaring, subterranean river boomed in the depths, felt as much as heard.
She called his name, and only a thin, hollow echo answered.
A deep, fathomless chasm split the floor in two; the stone he dropped into it never landed.
The stale, musty air tasted of earth and of ages without wind.
Behind the waterfall lay a hidden, glistening grotto, its walls sheathed in mineral like the inside of a shell.
In the wavering, feeble torchlight, the shadows moved when nothing else did.
He wedged himself into a tight, claustrophobic crevice and waited for the footsteps to pass.
It was cool and utterly peaceful inside, the only sound the unhurried drip of water finding its way through stone.
No daylight had ever reached this chamber; no voice had troubled it for a thousand years.
With a crack like thunder, part of the roof gave way, and rubble poured into the passage behind them.
Stalagmites rose from the floor like a forest of pale candles, each one gleaming where the light touched it.
